title: Semisimplicity ascends along isogenies of connected smooth affine groups
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $H_1,H_2$ be smooth connected affine $F$-group schemes of finite type, and let $f:H_1\to H_2$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism whose scheme-theoretic kernel has finite-dimensional coordinate algebra. If $H_2$ is semisimple, then $H_1$ is semisimple. Here semisimple means smooth, connected, affine, of finite type, and having no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme; solvable means that successive derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. The derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ factors. Faithfully flat means that the induced map of coordinate algebras makes the target algebra a faithfully flat module: extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semisimple-isogeny-invariance] with $G_1=H_1$, $G_0=H_2$ and the given $f$. Its affine finite-type smooth connected hypotheses are precisely those assumed here. Its faithfully flat condition is the stated faithfully flat coordinate-algebra condition. Its finite-kernel condition is exactly finite-dimensionality of the coordinate algebra of the scheme-theoretic kernel. Both statements define semisimplicity by the absence of nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup schemes and define solvability by termination of the derived subgroup series, with the same commutator-generated derived subgroup. Thus every hypothesis of the cited result is present, and its conclusion says $H_1$ is semisimple. No smoothness, reducedness or centrality of the kernel is imposed.

Milne states it for an isogeny φ: G'→G of connected group varieties. Its proof: the image of a smooth connected normal subgroup is normal (φ is surjective) and trivial, so the subgroup is finite, and it is then trivial because it is smooth and connected. For affine groups an isogeny is a faithfully flat map with finite kernel, so the item's hypotheses are exactly Milne's over F̄, and the statement is true. Edge cases checked: the identity map, trivial groups, SL_p→PGL_p in characteristic p with non-reduced kernel μ_p, and G_m×S→S, which is excluded by the finite-kernel hypothesis.
